# Radoslav Radev Recommends Mini Progressions Between Progressions Held for 6, 7, 8, 9 Seconds, 10 Seconds to Prevent Injuries

Radoslav Radev recommends using mini progressions between the main progressions and holding them for 6, 7, 8, 9 seconds, 10 seconds so the transition is much easier and less risky. [src: vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 03:24]

## Details

- Have mini progressions between the progressions and hold, for example, 6, 7, 8, 9 seconds, 10 seconds on the mini progression, and then the transition will be much easier and you are not risking that much. [src: vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 03:24]
- For planche, instead of going from advanced to straddle planche directly, do frog sandwich, rise at legs, pike, half pike, half advanced pike. [src: vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 03:39]
- For front lever, do not go directly from advanced front lever to full front lever; go from advanced to one leg, to one leg on advanced front lever, straddle front lever, baby straddle front lever, full front lever. [src: vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 04:05]
- Mini progressions are good for activation to feel the muscles, because going from tuck directly to advanced means you cannot feel your muscles or control your body. [src: vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 03:47]

## Evidence

- vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 03:24 (Radoslav Radev): "to have mini progressions between the progressions and not just to hold two seconds on the mini progression, but to hold again, let's say, 6, 7, 8, 9 seconds, 10 seconds on the mini progression, and then the transition will be much easier, and you're not risking that much."
- vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 03:39 (Radoslav Radev): "You're not risking to go, for example, from advanced to straddle planche, you're doing frog sandwich rise at legs, pike, half pike, half advanced pike."
- vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 04:05 (Radoslav Radev): "On the front lever as well, don't go directly from advanced front lever to full front lever. You can go from advanced to one leg to one leg on advanced front lever, straddle front lever, baby straddle front lever, full front lever."
- vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 03:47 (Radoslav Radev): "Also, it's really good for the activation to feel the muscles, because if you have to go from tuck directly to advanced, you're not feeling your muscles, you can't control your body."

## Why This Matters

He says that the smallest thing that can happen from skipping mini progressions is losing protraction or collapsing, but the worst is injury. [src: vid-3EcXfOgjk1o @ 03:56]
